phase1_leaf_result.part121_scope: One bounded 24-cell model comparing unprotected ref, default protected branch, and admin-enforced/empty-bypass repository protection across direct rewind/delete, policy edit/delete, repository deletion, stale claimant, response-loss retry, rate-limit interruption, and concurrent CAS.
phase1_leaf_result.new_narrowing: Strong repository-local protection reduced direct-ref mutation to 0/2 unsafe but remained 2/2 unsafe for meta-policy/repository-lifecycle attacks because repository admins/edit-rules roles can change/delete repository rules and admins/owners can delete the repository. Same-object CAS remains one-winner/idempotent only while repository identity/history is current.
phase1_leaf_result.minimal_unresolved_child: Can least-privileged worker credentials plus a stable repository-identity fence safely narrow the threat model to worker-originated effects while failing closed on owner/admin policy or repository-lifecycle changes, without an external monotonic witness?

phase1_acceptance.scope_guard: Only current multi_agent own state and current official public GitHub protected-branch/ruleset/repository-deletion documentation; no O, other-role, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, scheduler or protected-primary semantic input/effect.

continuation: Part122: execute one bounded least-privilege authority-separation model. Compare worker token/App permissions limited to contents, worker credentials with administration, and repository-owner lifecycle authority across force-push, rule edit/delete, repository delete/recreate, token rotation/revocation, stale claimant, response-loss retry, and rate-limit interruption. Require a stable repository-identity check and fail closed on identity/policy uncertainty. Determine whether narrowing the threat model to worker-originated effects yields a zero-cost public-free repository-local candidate without claiming safety against owner/admin compromise; persist one checkpoint and no second leaf.
